headline: ML-guided transcriptomics nominates candidate genes in cancer and immune disease
label: Machine Learning Gene Prioritization
summary: Public single-cell and bulk transcriptomes are now routinely paired with machine learning to prioritize candidate genes and response signatures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is public transcriptomic data, frequently at single-cell resolution, used to nominate candidate genes through differential expression or WGCNA combined with machine learning feature selection, typically followed by bioinformatic or experimental validation. Most items address cancer, including a pan-cancer oxidative stress signature in cancer-associated fibroblasts (FOSR.Sig) predicting immunotherapy response, a programmed cell death learning signature with AP1S1 in breast cancer, and ZNF385A in small cell lung cancer, while others address keloid, hypertrophic scarring, periodontitis, osteoarthritis, and rheumatoid arthritis with tuberculosis. Some studies extend beyond expression profiling: a neoantigen prognostic model for gastric adenocarcinoma includes mRNA vaccine designs, and spatial transcriptomics is paired with Mendelian randomization in endometrial cancer. Novelty lies mainly in specific gene nominations, such as TOP2A acting through TGF-β2/Smad signaling in OSCC, and in integrated data layers rather than in the analytic framework itself.
